PRFL-220.name: Theatre Ensemble
PRFL-220.description: Participates in faculty-directed or mentored campus theatre productions as performers, designers or technicians, with writing, creation and text analysis.
notes: No separate prerequisite field was displayed; this does not establish unrestricted enrollment.
The actual card is one credit. Route-level repetition/accumulation rules must not be replaced by an inferred three-credit course.

category_review.locator: PRFL-220 / complete public popup / 2026–2027 theatre arts immersion
category_review.rationale: Substantive theatre-production practice is the central activity.

PRFL-221.name: Fundamentals of Acting
PRFL-221.description: Combines acting history and theory with vocal and physical exercises, scene work, textual analysis and character development.
notes: No separate prerequisite field was displayed; this does not establish unrestricted enrollment.

category_review.locator: PRFL-221 / complete public popup / 2026–2027 theatre arts immersion
category_review.rationale: The source explicitly balances historical/theoretical study and practical acting techniques.

PRFL-222.name: Improv & Storytelling
PRFL-222.description: Develops improvised performance through scene creation, physical storytelling, character work and ensemble collaboration.
notes: No separate prerequisite field was displayed; this does not establish unrestricted enrollment.

category_review.locator: PRFL-222 / complete public popup / 2026–2027 theatre arts immersion
category_review.rationale: Crafting theatrical performances is the core artistic practice; communication supports that production.

PRFL-227.name: Dramatic Theory and Text Analysis
PRFL-227.description: Studies major dramatic and performance theories and applies them to play interpretation from production perspectives.
notes: No separate prerequisite field was displayed; this does not establish unrestricted enrollment.

category_review.locator: PRFL-227 / complete public popup / 2026–2027 theatre arts immersion
category_review.rationale: The stated work centers on theoretical and textual interpretation.

PRFL-230.name: Devising Theatre: Creating Ensemble Based Performance
PRFL-230.description: Creates original or adapted ensemble theatre through collaborative exercises, workshops, writing and presentations informed by theatre history and social-change theory.
notes: No separate prerequisite field was displayed; this does not establish unrestricted enrollment.

category_review.locator: PRFL-230 / complete public popup / 2026–2027 theatre arts immersion
category_review.rationale: Hands-on creation of theatrical pieces is the organizing activity.

PRFL-235.name: Fundamentals of Musical Theatre
PRFL-235.description: Analyzes musical-theatre songs as narrative, music and cultural artifacts, then develops interpretations through performance.
notes: No separate prerequisite field was displayed; this does not establish unrestricted enrollment.

category_review.locator: PRFL-235 / complete public popup / 2026–2027 theatre arts immersion
category_review.rationale: The source deliberately combines cultural/textual interpretation and substantive performance practice.

PRFL-319.name: Themes in Theatre Studies
PRFL-319.description: Investigates an announced theatre-history or theory topic through research, cultural interpretation and offering-specific projects or performances.
notes: No separate prerequisite field was displayed; this does not establish unrestricted enrollment.
Topic and research deliverable vary; the topic is announced before the offering.

category_review.locator: PRFL-319 / complete public popup / 2026–2027 theatre arts immersion
category_review.rationale: The stated scope is theatre history, play analysis and cultural frameworks; possible performances are research deliverables.

PRFL-320.name: Dramaturgy
PRFL-320.description: Develops collaborative interpretation of plays and communicates research and creative choices through analyses, program notes, guides and dialogue.
notes: No separate prerequisite field was displayed; this does not establish unrestricted enrollment.

category_review.locator: PRFL-320 / complete public popup / 2026–2027 theatre arts immersion
category_review.rationale: Interpretation and communication of dramatic research are the explicit skills.

PRFL-321.name: Traditions of Theatre in Europe
PRFL-321.description: Examines selected European plays and productions in historical, artistic and theoretical contexts; periods and national traditions vary.
notes: No separate prerequisite field was displayed; this does not establish unrestricted enrollment.

category_review.locator: PRFL-321 / complete public popup / 2026–2027 theatre arts immersion
category_review.rationale: Historical and cultural interpretation of theatrical traditions is the stated focus.

PRFL-323.name: Traditions of Shakespearean Theatre
PRFL-323.description: Studies Shakespearean genres and dramatic language as potential productions, combining interpretation with oral performance, staging exercises and collaborative scene work.
notes: No separate prerequisite field was displayed; this does not establish unrestricted enrollment.

category_review.locator: PRFL-323 / complete public popup / 2026–2027 theatre arts immersion
category_review.rationale: The source combines literary and historical interpretation with substantive staging and performance practice.

PRFL-327.name: American Musical Theater
PRFL-327.description: Surveys American musical theatre through representative works, creators and performers, developing historical appreciation and critical evaluation.
notes: No separate prerequisite field was displayed; this does not establish unrestricted enrollment.

category_review.locator: PRFL-327 / complete public popup / 2026–2027 theatre arts immersion
category_review.rationale: Historical study and critical appreciation organize the course, rather than a stated studio-production sequence.

PRFL-330.name: Performing Identity in Popular Media
PRFL-330.description: Examines identity construction and everyday politics through popular media, theoretical readings, films, discussion and critical writing.
notes: No separate prerequisite field was displayed; this does not establish unrestricted enrollment.

category_review.locator: PRFL-330 / complete public popup / 2026–2027 theatre arts immersion
category_review.rationale: Identity, culture and critical interpretation are central; the title does not establish an artistic studio course.

PRFL-331.name: Fundamentals of Directing
PRFL-331.description: Develops a director’s process from script analysis through concept, rehearsal and staging, culminating in a staged scene or short play with feedback.
notes: No separate prerequisite field was displayed; this does not establish unrestricted enrollment.

category_review.locator: PRFL-331 / complete public popup / 2026–2027 theatre arts immersion
category_review.rationale: Directing and producing staged work are the central practical activities; textual analysis supports them.

PRFN-200.name: Appreciation of Theatrical Design
PRFN-200.description: Studies theatrical design, personnel and aesthetics through cultural history, scripts, scenic space, lighting, costume, accessibility and Deaf theatre.
notes: No separate prerequisite field was displayed; this does not establish unrestricted enrollment.
The card states that no artistic or technical skills are necessary; this is not a general enrollment eligibility guarantee.

category_review.locator: PRFN-200 / complete public popup / 2026–2027 theatre arts immersion
category_review.rationale: The course emphasizes appreciation and interpretation of design; the source explicitly does not require artistic or technical skills.

PRFN-204.name: Scenic Painting and Props
PRFN-204.description: Practices theatrical painting and prop-making methods through individual and group projects, using relevant materials, techniques and communication tools.
notes: No separate prerequisite field was displayed; this does not establish unrestricted enrollment.

category_review.locator: PRFN-204 / complete public popup / 2026–2027 theatre arts immersion
category_review.rationale: Project-based production of theatrical painting and props is explicit substantive artistic practice.

PRFN-240.name: Dance History
PRFN-240.description: Studies dance traditions and experimental forms in historical, cultural and social contexts using readings, discussion, viewing and reflection.
notes: No separate prerequisite field was displayed; this does not establish unrestricted enrollment.

category_review.locator: PRFN-240 / complete public popup / 2026–2027 theatre arts immersion
category_review.rationale: Dance history, theory and cultural interpretation organize the stated learning.

PRFN-243.name: Dance: Jazz
PRFN-243.description: Combines jazz dance movement, improvisation and rhythmic practice with theory, history, cultural perspectives and reflective reading and writing.
notes: No separate prerequisite field was displayed; this does not establish unrestricted enrollment.
Four lecture/lab contact hours are not four course credits.

category_review.locator: PRFN-243 / complete public popup / 2026–2027 theatre-arts immersion
category_review.rationale: The description combines substantial dance practice with explicit historical and cultural study.

PRFN-244.name: Dance: Hip Hop
PRFN-244.description: Combines hip-hop movement, conditioning and style exploration with historical, aesthetic and cultural study, discussion and writing.
notes: No separate prerequisite field was displayed; this does not establish unrestricted enrollment.
Four lecture/lab contact hours are not four course credits.

category_review.locator: PRFN-244 / complete public popup / 2026–2027 theatre-arts immersion
category_review.rationale: The description presents both movement practice and historical/cultural interpretation as substantive work.

PRFN-246.name: Dance: Modern
PRFN-246.description: Introduces modern dance technique, rhythm, improvisation and choreography through movement practice informed by historical and cultural perspectives.
notes: No separate prerequisite field was displayed; this does not establish unrestricted enrollment.
The card explicitly says that no previous dance experience is required.
Four lecture/lab contact hours are not four course credits.

category_review.locator: PRFN-246 / complete public popup / 2026–2027 theatre-arts immersion
category_review.rationale: Creation and execution of dance are central, with theoretical context supporting the artistic practice.

PRFN-247.name: Dance: Ballet
PRFN-247.description: Develops ballet technique, alignment, phrasing and movement awareness through practice, with aesthetic, historical and cultural context.
notes: No separate prerequisite field was displayed; this does not establish unrestricted enrollment.
The card explicitly says that no previous dance experience is required.
Four lecture/lab contact hours are not four course credits.

category_review.locator: PRFN-247 / complete public popup / 2026–2027 theatre-arts immersion
category_review.rationale: The source explicitly identifies individual dance technique and ballet movement as its primary focus.

PRFL-250.name: Music History 1: Antiquity to Bach
PRFL-250.description: Studies music from antiquity to about 1750 in cultural, religious, political and artistic contexts, including notation, instruments, audiences and criticism.
notes: No separate prerequisite field was displayed; this does not establish unrestricted enrollment.

category_review.locator: PRFL-250 / complete public popup / 2026–2027 music immersion
category_review.rationale: Historical and critical interpretation of music is central.

PRFL-251.name: Music History 2: Haydn to Stravinsky
PRFL-251.description: Studies music from about 1750 to 1920 in social, cultural and aesthetic contexts, including nationalism, instruments, popular traditions and criticism.
PRFL-251.prerequisites: FNRT-110 or PRFL-160 or PRFL-250 or FNRT-205 or PRFL-265 or equivalent course.

category_review.locator: PRFL-251 / complete public popup / 2026–2027 music immersion
category_review.rationale: The stated work is historical and cultural interpretation of music.

PRFL-262.name: Music & Global Cultures
PRFL-262.description: Uses ethnomusicology to examine music as cultural practice through listening, musical and rhythmic analysis, ethnographic readings, discussion and writing.
notes: No separate prerequisite field was displayed; this does not establish unrestricted enrollment.

category_review.locator: PRFL-262 / complete public popup / 2026–2027 music immersion
category_review.rationale: Music’s social meaning and cultural interpretation are the organizing focus.

PRFL-263.name: American Popular & Rock Music
PRFL-263.description: Surveys American popular and rock music, especially the postwar period, through styles, representative performers and basic musical analysis.
notes: No separate prerequisite field was displayed; this does not establish unrestricted enrollment.

category_review.locator: PRFL-263 / complete public popup / 2026–2027 music immersion
category_review.rationale: Historical survey and critical listening dominate rather than a stated performance studio.

PRFL-264.name: Music & the Stage
PRFL-264.description: Surveys historical and cultural collaboration between music and theatre through selected works spanning opera, drama, cabaret and musical comedy.
notes: No separate prerequisite field was displayed; this does not establish unrestricted enrollment.

category_review.locator: PRFL-264 / complete public popup / 2026–2027 music immersion
category_review.rationale: The stated activity is historical and cultural study of works, not producing performances.

PRFL-265.name: Music Theory 1
PRFL-265.description: Develops melody, counterpoint, harmony and musicianship while analyzing musical form and style, with work adapted to students’ skills.
notes: The description expects basic literacy in music notation; this is a prose expectation, not a displayed separately labeled prerequisite field.

category_review.locator: PRFL-265 / complete public popup / 2026–2027 music immersion
category_review.rationale: Composition and musicianship are substantive artistic practices supported by formal analysis.

PRFL-280.name: RIT Singers
PRFL-280.description: Learns choral repertoire spanning several centuries through rehearsals and concert performance, with theory, historical context and small-ensemble opportunities.
PRFL-280.prerequisites: Auditions will be held to assess proper placement. Contact the instructor for information. Students who have previously participated in RIT Singers can enroll without further permission.
notes: The actual course range is 0–1 credits; no single credit amount is inferred from route totals or contact hours.

category_review.locator: PRFL-280 / complete public popup / 2026–2027 music immersion
category_review.rationale: Rehearsal and musical performance are the central practical activities; historical and analytical context supports that work.

PRFL-281.name: RIT Philharmonic Orchestra
PRFL-281.description: Rehearses and performs orchestral repertoire spanning several centuries, with opportunities to play chamber music.
PRFL-281.prerequisites: Auditions will be held to assess proper placement. Contact the instructor for information. Students who have previously participated in RIT Orchestra can enroll without further permission.
notes: The actual course range is 0–1 credits; no single credit amount is inferred from route totals or contact hours.

category_review.locator: PRFL-281 / complete public popup / 2026–2027 music immersion
category_review.rationale: Rehearsal and musical performance are the central practical activities; historical and analytical context supports that work.

PRFL-282.name: RIT Concert Band
PRFL-282.description: Learns and performs wind-band repertoire, including contemporary works, marches and transcriptions, with theory and historical context.
PRFL-282.prerequisites: Auditions will be held to assess proper placement. Contact the instructor for information. Students who have previously participated in RIT Concert Band can enroll without further permission.
notes: The actual course range is 0–1 credits; no single credit amount is inferred from route totals or contact hours.

category_review.locator: PRFL-282 / complete public popup / 2026–2027 music immersion
category_review.rationale: Rehearsal and musical performance are the central practical activities; historical and analytical context supports that work.

PRFL-283.name: West African Percussion Ensemble
PRFL-283.description: Practices Guinean ensemble drumming through interlocking percussion parts, accompaniment and solo technique, emphasizing cooperation.
notes: No separate prerequisite field was displayed; this does not establish unrestricted enrollment.
The actual course range is 0–1 credits; no single credit amount is inferred from route totals or contact hours.
The description explicitly opens enrollment to interested students, faculty and staff regardless of musical proficiency.

category_review.locator: PRFL-283 / complete public popup / 2026–2027 music immersion
category_review.rationale: Rehearsal and musical performance are the central practical activities; historical and analytical context supports that work.

PRFL-284.name: RIT Jazz Ensemble
PRFL-284.description: Prepares and performs jazz repertoire, using analysis and comparison of works to develop musicianship and cultural appreciation.
PRFL-284.prerequisites: Auditions will be held to assess proper placement. Contact the instructor for information. Students who have previously participated in RIT Jazz Ensemble can enroll without further permission.
notes: The actual course range is 0–1 credits; no single credit amount is inferred from route totals or contact hours.

category_review.locator: PRFL-284 / complete public popup / 2026–2027 music immersion
category_review.rationale: Rehearsal and musical performance are the central practical activities; historical and analytical context supports that work.

PRFL-285.name: RIT Chamber Orchestra
PRFL-285.description: Performs selected orchestral repertoire and explores historical performing practices, stylistic interpretation and revival of earlier works.
PRFL-285.prerequisites: Auditions will be held to assess proper placement. Contact the instructor for information. Students who have previously participated in RIT Chamber Orchestra can enroll without further permission.
notes: The actual course range is 0–1 credits; no single credit amount is inferred from route totals or contact hours.
The description also specifies invitation by the music director or audition; prior participants are addressed separately in the eligibility field.

category_review.locator: PRFL-285 / complete public popup / 2026–2027 music immersion
category_review.rationale: Rehearsal and musical performance are the central practical activities; historical and analytical context supports that work.

PRFL-352.name: Russian Music and National Identity
PRFL-352.description: Examines Russian musical nationalism and cultural exchange through historical, political and aesthetic research, analysis and persuasive writing.
notes: No separate prerequisite field was displayed; this does not establish unrestricted enrollment.

category_review.locator: PRFL-352 / complete public popup / 2026–2027 music immersion
category_review.rationale: The writing-intensive historical seminar centers on culture, identity and interpretation.

PRFL-372.name: Survey of Jazz
PRFL-372.description: Surveys jazz history through representative creators and works, emphasizing multiracial influences and relationships with American culture.
notes: No separate prerequisite field was displayed; this does not establish unrestricted enrollment.

category_review.locator: PRFL-372 / complete public popup / 2026–2027 music immersion
category_review.rationale: Historical and cultural analysis is the explicit focus.

PRFL-376.name: History & Technology of Musical Instruments
PRFL-376.description: Studies the historical development of instruments, manufacturing techniques, sound expectations and comparative performing practices.
notes: No separate prerequisite field was displayed; this does not establish unrestricted enrollment.

category_review.locator: PRFL-376 / complete public popup / 2026–2027 music immersion
category_review.rationale: Technology is examined historically in musical culture; the description does not promise engineering design instruction.

PRFL-465.name: Music Theory 2
PRFL-465.description: Advances melodic and contrapuntal development, harmony, chromatic materials, modulation and analysis while developing individual musical skills.
notes: The description also expects basic music theory and understanding of four-part diatonic composition.

category_review.locator: PRFL-465 / complete public popup / 2026–2027 music immersion
category_review.rationale: Advanced composition and musicianship are substantive artistic practices.

PRFN-101.name: Introduction to Accessibility and Inclusion in the Performing Arts
PRFN-101.description: Studies accessibility, disability, representation and inclusive design in theatre and dance, combining critical perspectives with creative captioning, movement and sensory storytelling.
PRFN-101.prerequisites: This course is open to all students in AAS, AS, BS, BFA or NTID pre-baccalaureate (PBENG-UND, PBSCI-UND, PBLIBL-UND, PBCOM-UND) programs.

category_review.locator: PRFN-101 / complete public popup / 2026–2027 theatre-design-and-stagecraft immersion
category_review.rationale: Both critical accessibility theory and hands-on inclusive artistic practices are explicitly developed.

PRFN-201.name: Appreciation of Media in Performance
PRFN-201.description: Studies the history, theory and expressive use of performance media, including technology, Deaf theatre and inclusive storytelling.
notes: No separate prerequisite field was displayed; this does not establish unrestricted enrollment.

category_review.locator: PRFN-201 / complete public popup / 2026–2027 theatre-design-and-stagecraft immersion
category_review.rationale: Appreciation and historical/theoretical interpretation are stated; no technical media-production project is promised.

PRFN-207.name: Appreciation of Theatrical Costumes
PRFN-207.description: Introduces costume design through artistic, historical and technical concepts, materials and equipment, with attention to performance meaning and Deaf theatre.
notes: No separate prerequisite field was displayed; this does not establish unrestricted enrollment.

category_review.locator: PRFN-207 / complete public popup / 2026–2027 theatre-design-and-stagecraft immersion
category_review.rationale: The source frames the work as appreciation and interpretation of design; it does not specify a costume-construction studio.

PRFN-208.name: Appreciation of Theatrical Scenery
PRFN-208.description: Examines scenic design principles, tools, history and technology through creative expression and diverse performance traditions.
notes: No separate prerequisite field was displayed; this does not establish unrestricted enrollment.

category_review.locator: PRFN-208 / complete public popup / 2026–2027 theatre-design-and-stagecraft immersion
category_review.rationale: The stated focus is study and appreciation of theatrical design, without an explicit build or studio requirement.

PRFN-209.name: Appreciation of Theatrical Lighting
PRFN-209.description: Studies theatrical lighting techniques and equipment in historical, expressive and cultural contexts, including Deaf theatre.
notes: No separate prerequisite field was displayed; this does not establish unrestricted enrollment.

category_review.locator: PRFN-209 / complete public popup / 2026–2027 theatre-design-and-stagecraft immersion
category_review.rationale: Lighting is introduced through study and appreciation; the card does not establish a lighting-production practicum.

PRFN-303.name: Semiotics of the Visual in Performing Arts
PRFN-303.description: Analyzes how visual elements, movement and signed language create performance meaning across traditions, periods and cultures.

category_review.locator: PRFN-303 / complete public popup / 2026–2027 theatre-design-and-stagecraft immersion
category_review.rationale: Communication, interpretation and writing are explicit core activities.

PRFN-316.name: Playwriting I
PRFN-316.description: Develops short scripts through dramatic structure, dialogue, character work, revision and peer critique, alongside reading plays by Deaf and hearing writers.

category_review.locator: PRFN-316 / complete public popup / 2026–2027 theatre-design-and-stagecraft immersion
category_review.rationale: Creative writing and textual communication map to human context even when the writing is for theatre.

PRFN-403.name: Performance Studies
PRFN-403.description: Uses interdisciplinary concepts to analyze staged performances and everyday social practices, including identity, ritual and signed communication.

category_review.locator: PRFN-403 / complete public popup / 2026–2027 theatre-design-and-stagecraft immersion
category_review.rationale: Cultural interpretation, social meaning and writing organize the course.

PRFN-250.name: Choreography: Designing Movement
PRFN-250.description: Studies choreography and movement design through historical, cultural and theoretical perspectives, examining live performance and digitally produced examples.
notes: No separate prerequisite field was displayed; this does not establish unrestricted enrollment.
Four lecture/lab contact hours are not four course credits.

category_review.locator: PRFN-250 / complete public popup / 2026–2027 dance immersion
category_review.rationale: The source promises study and appreciation of movement design, not an explicit choreography-production project.

PRFN-340.name: World Dance & Culture
PRFN-340.description: Examines world dance traditions through active experience and cross-cultural historical, critical and social analysis.
PRFN-340.prerequisites: PRFN-240 or PRFN-243 or PRFN-244 or PRFN-246 or PRFN-247 or PRFN-250 or equivalent course.

category_review.locator: PRFN-340 / complete public popup / 2026–2027 dance immersion
category_review.rationale: The description combines active dance experience with substantial cross-cultural interpretation.

PRFN-341.name: Exploring Technology in Dance
PRFN-341.description: Investigates historical and contemporary uses of technology in creating and producing dance through inquiry and critical appreciation.
PRFN-341.prerequisites: PRFN-240 or PRFN-243 or PRFN-244 or PRFN-246 or PRFN-247 or PRFN-250 or equivalent course.

category_review.locator: PRFN-341 / complete public popup / 2026–2027 dance immersion
category_review.rationale: The stated work examines the relationship of dance and technology; it does not establish programming or engineering instruction.

PRFN-342.name: African Dance
PRFN-342.description: Studies regional African dance and movement through participation and analysis of historical, cultural and social significance.
notes: No separate prerequisite field was displayed; this does not establish unrestricted enrollment.

category_review.locator: PRFN-342 / complete public popup / 2026–2027 dance immersion
category_review.rationale: Both embodied dance participation and cultural interpretation are explicit.

PRFN-345.name: Movement Analysis and Visual Expression
PRFN-345.description: Explores dance and movement behavior through embodied creative work, connecting emotional, physical and cognitive processes with self-awareness.
PRFN-345.prerequisites: PRFN-240 or PRFN-243 or PRFN-244 or PRFN-246 or PRFN-247 or PRFN-250 or equivalent course.

category_review.locator: PRFN-345 / complete public popup / 2026–2027 dance immersion
category_review.rationale: First-person movement and creative bodily expression are explicit central practices.

PRFN-214.name: Appreciation of Artistic Sign Language
PRFN-214.description: Analyzes artistic sign language in screen and stage work, including translation, Deaf and hearing performance, accessibility and critical evaluation.
PRFN-214.prerequisites: MLAS-301 or INTP-126 or NASL-200 or equivalent course or a minimum score of 3 on the ASL placement exam.
notes: Instruction is in ASL; the card states that voice interpreters will not be provided.

category_review.locator: PRFN-214 / complete public popup / 2026–2027 american-sign-language-and-deaf-cultural-studies immersion
category_review.rationale: Language, translation and critical interpretation are the stated focus.

PRFN-314.name: ASL Musicality
PRFN-314.description: Examines visual musical expression, sign-language poetics and Deaf artists through readings and analysis of ASL performance and music videos.
notes: Instruction is in ASL; the card states that voice interpreters will not be provided.

category_review.locator: PRFN-314 / complete public popup / 2026–2027 american-sign-language-and-deaf-cultural-studies immersion
category_review.rationale: Language, aesthetics, history and interpretation organize the work; no performance-production requirement is stated.

PRFL-379.name: History of Electronic Music
PRFL-379.description: Studies electronic music’s technological and cultural history through listening, analysis, journals and model composition projects.
notes: No separate prerequisite field was displayed; this does not establish unrestricted enrollment.
The description does not require an extensive music background. Mention of artificial intelligence as a historical tool does not establish an AI-methods course.

category_review.locator: PRFL-379 / complete public popup / 2026–2027 american-arts immersion
category_review.rationale: The source combines historical and aesthetic interpretation with substantive model composition practice.
